name: query_module
synopsis: int query_module(const char *name, int which, void *buf, size_t bufsize, size_t *ret);
description: query_module() requests information from the kernel about loadable modules. The returned information is placed in a user-provided buffer, and the caller must specify the buffer size. The exact nature of the information depends on the operation specified by the which parameter.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the module to query, or NULL for the kernel proper.

parameters.name: which
parameters.description: Specifies the operation to perform, such as QM_MODULES or QM_INFO.

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer to hold the returned information.

parameters.name: bufsize
parameters.description: Size of the buffer pointed to by buf.

parameters.name: ret
parameters.description: Pointer to return additional information, such as the number of items or minimum buffer size needed.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: At least one of name, buf, or ret was outside the program’s accessible address space.
Invalid which; or name is NULL, but this is not permitted with the specified value of which.
No module by that name exists.
The buffer size provided was too small; ret is set to the minimum size needed.
query_module() is not supported in this version of the kernel (e.g., Linux 2.6 or later).

bugs: This system call is deprecated and removed in Linux 2.6 and later, making it unavailable in modern kernels.
